topic: The Antarctic ozone hole — what the 47-year record actually shows
reader_question: Is the ozone layer really recovering, and how would anyone know?

sources.title: NASA Ozone Watch — Annual Records (Antarctic)
sources.what_it_gives: The complete annual table used by every chart in this special: maximum daily ozone-hole area (million km2) and minimum daily column ozone (DU) for 1979-2025, plus the 07 Sep-13 Oct seasonal mean area and the 21 Sep-16 Oct mean minimum ozone. Page states there are no data for 1995 and asks to credit 'NASA Ozone Watch'.
sources.confidence: primary data provider (satellite + ground-based merged record)

sources.title: NASA Ozone Watch — What is the Ozone Hole?
sources.what_it_gives: The measurement definition: total column ozone below 220 Dobson Units is used as the boundary of the hole because values under 220 DU were not observed before 1979 and are known from aircraft campaigns to result from chlorine- and bromine-catalysed loss. Also the mechanism (polar vortex, polar stratospheric clouds, chlorine reservoir conversion, catalytic destruction).

sources.title: NASA Ozone Watch — What is Ozone?
sources.what_it_gives: Stratospheric context: 90% of atmospheric ozone sits between about 10 and 50 km; total mass about 3 billion metric tonnes = 0.00006% of the atmosphere; peak concentration near 32 km; ozone screens all UV-C and most UV-B but only about half of UV-A.

sources.title: UNEP Ozone Secretariat — Facts and figures on ozone protection
sources.what_it_gives: Treaty and benefit figures used in the special: 198 Parties; nearly 100 controlled ODSs; 99% of ODSs phased out (about 1.8 million ODP tonnes); return to 1980 column-ozone values around 2066 (Antarctic), 2045 (Arctic), 2040 (60N-60S); 135 billion tonnes CO2-equivalent avoided 1990-2010; 0.5-1 C avoided warming by mid-century; upper-stratosphere ozone +1.5-2.2% per decade at mid-latitudes and lower tropical stratosphere -1-2% per decade (2000-2020); UV-B up to a factor of five without the Protocol; UV index +10-20% at latitudes under 50 degrees, +25% at the southern tip of South America, over +100% at the South Pole in spring; US EPA estimate of 443 million skin-cancer cases, 2.3 million skin-cancer deaths and 63 million cataract cases prevented for people born 1890-2100; Multilateral Fund contributions near US$5.1 billion as of May 2023; US$1.8 trillion health benefits and about US$460 billion avoided damage to agriculture, fisheries and materials (1987-2060); average global warming impact of 22 widely used HFCs about 2,500 times CO2; Kigali phases down 18 HFCs by more than 80% in CO2-equivalent; Kigali avoids 0.3-0.5 C by 2100.
sources.confidence: treaty secretariat compilation; the EPA health figures are that agency's modelled estimate

sources.title: Scientific Assessment of Ozone Depletion: 2022 — Executive Summary
sources.publisher: WMO / UNEP Scientific Assessment Panel (hosted by NOAA CSL), GAW Report No. 278
sources.what_it_gives: The peer-reviewed trends used here: near-global (60S-60N) total column ozone +0.3% per decade over 1996-2020 with a 2-sigma uncertainty of at least +/-0.3; Southern Hemisphere mid-latitudes +0.8 +/- 0.7; Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes 0.0 +/- 0.7; tropics +0.2 +/- 0.3; present-day column ozone still about 2% (near-global), 4% (NH mid-latitudes) and 5% (SH mid-latitudes) below the 1964-1980 average; Antarctic springtime return to 1980 values about 2065, possibly about 2050 under low-mitigation scenarios; Arctic about 2045; NH mid-latitudes about 2035; near-global about 2040; unreported CFC-11 production over 2012-2019 is estimated to delay polar ozone return by up to 3 years and global return by about 1 year; HFC radiative forcing reached 0.044 +/- 0.006 W m-2 in 2020; HFC emissions in 2050 projected at 0.9-1.0 Gt CO2-eq/yr with the Kigali Amendment versus 4.0-5.3 without controls; upper-stratosphere ozone trends 1.5-2.2% per decade at mid-latitudes and 1.1-1.6% per decade in the tropics for 2000-2020; lower-stratosphere mid-latitude trends are not robust across datasets and models.
sources.confidence: highest available (quadrennial peer-reviewed assessment, ~230 scientists, 30 countries)

sources.title: The Kigali Amendment: An overview
sources.what_it_gives: Kigali adoption 2016, entry into force 1 January 2019; HFCs were about 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions and growing at over 10% per year without controls; developed countries began reductions in 2019; global HFC use expected to fall 80-85% by 2047; up to 0.5 C of warming avoided by 2100, potentially about 1 C when combined with energy-efficiency improvements; more than 170 countries had ratified as of the page's last update.

not_verified_or_not_used: I did not obtain NOAA's measurement-level CFC-11 emissions series, so work 07 quotes only the WMO 2022 assessment statement (source S5) and the UNEP line on unexplained emissions; no CFC-11 concentration curve is drawn.

The seasonal (month-by-month) shape of the hole in work 04 is drawn from the documented August-October spring cycle in source S2 and the seasonal windows used in the NASA table (07 Sep-13 Oct; 21 Sep-16 Oct). It is labelled a schematic, not a data plot.
No 2026 figure is used anywhere: NASA Ozone Watch's table ends at 2025, and the site was last updated 2025-10-20.
fictional_or_illustrative_elements: Editorial furniture only: the special's masthead name ('Stratosphere Review'), its issue number and the fictional editor byline. No invented data, no invented measurements, no invented quotes.
Diagram proportions in works 01 and 05 (altitude bands, vortex geometry) are schematic illustrations of the published mechanism, not data plots, and are labelled as such on the sheet.
